PROBLEM 6A-1B:ANALYZE AN UNREINFORCED MASONRY WALL FOR
EXTERIOR BLAST LOAD
Solution:
Step 1.
Given:
a.
The design blast pressure history from a far range, exterior
explosion has the same shape shown in Figure 6A-1a (+), except
the peak pressure is 1.4 psi and the duration is 40 milliseconds.
The wall will not be exposed to any fragmentation hazard and will
not be placed in net tension from static or blast loads.
b.
The 8 inch CMU wall spans vertically with simple supports at the
floor slab and roof diaphragm with a clear span of 120 inches. It
laterally supports a 4 inch brick non-structural veneer wall. The wall
must provide Protection Category 1. The wall has #4 rebar dowels
at 48 inches o.c. and a bond beam at the top. The CMU walls are
shear walls for the building, which has plan dimensions with an
aspect ratio of 2:1. The wall is ungrouted and is not a load-bearing
wall. Since the design criteria satisfy the direct shear requirements
of section 6-7.3.5,
,no direct shear check is required.
Step 2.
The wall is 8 in thick (nominal thickness), light weight, concrete masonry
units (CMU) without any steel reinforcement or grouted cells. Assume the
static compressive stress
is 1300 psi based a review of recommended
values for ungrouted CMU. The actual wall thickness Tis 7.63 inches.
Step 3.
Determine dynamic design stresses. (Table 6-2 (+))
Masonry:
Flexural tension (fdt) - 200 psi (per Section 6-7.3.3)
Step 4.
Determine the ultimate moment capacity of the wal

moment of inertia (I) from Table 6-1 (+)
b. Determine the ultimate moment capacity of the CMU wall based on the
flexural tension strength (ft) from Step 3 and the section modulus using
Equation 6-12. The axial load P is zero.
